messages:
infra-oncall: Heads-up — dedicated pool eu-west-2 (dedicated-eu-west2-gpu-pool-3) is at 98% util and we're seeing evictions and request queuing. Spillover to hosted kicked in automatically but a subset of low-tier routes are hitting 429s and some 504s. Investigating.

sophie: Oncall ack. I'm looking at pool capacity now, suspecting a sustained batch job pattern. Can someone check recent provisioning events?

ajay: I see repeated scale attempts from the scheduler at 2026-03-18T09:35Z — APIServer returned 409 overcommit. Logs: 
```
2026-03-18T09:35:12Z scale: target +4 nodes
2026-03-18T09:35:12Z api -> 409: quota.overcommit_denied
2026-03-18T09:35:15Z spillover: redirecting 1200 rps to hosted eu-west
```

maya: Routing note: Hosted accepts routed traffic but latency for small-gen chat is up ~120ms p90. We can temporarily change routing policy to prefer hosted for non-enterprise tenants to reduce queue depth in dedicated. Want me to flip?

infra-oncall: Yes please flip non-enterprise -> hosted for eu-west2. @deploy-bot initiate policy change and post rollback plan. Keep dedicated for enterprise and reserved routes.

deploy-bot: Running policy update: set route.pref_eu_west2.non_enterprise=hosted at 1778610105. Will monitor for 5m then confirm.

sophie: Quick mitigation: I found large training-like batch jobs from internal-ml-test project consuming slots. I've muted the ci-scheduler for that project for 15m to free capacity.

ajay: Tried to trigger burst-add again, here's the curl payload I used: 
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/pools/dedicated-eu-west2/actions/scale \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INFRATOKEN' \
 -d '{"target_type":"burst","nodes":4}'
```
Response still 409 (quota exhausted). We're blocked until provider quota refresh or we free nodes.

maya: After routing flip, queue length dropped ~60% for dedicated and hosted errors fell. p50 latency improves. Still seeing 504s for the long tail of requests that were queued >2s.

infra-runbook-bot: Runbook suggested steps executed: 1) spillover enabled (automated) 2) non-enterprise routing flip (manual) 3) noisy-tenant throttled (manual). Next recommended: assess reserved capacity and file a ticket for capacity increase.

infra-oncall: Action items: (1) Sophie keep noisy tenant muted until stable (2) Ajay open capacity-increase request with cloud team and include recent utilization + cost delta (3) Maya watch routing metrics and revert if errors spike on hosted (4) Infra to notify support A/B routes to customers impacted.

sophie: Opening internal bug and tagging cloud-quota-team now. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/RI-2026-487

ajay: Putting a temporary manual eviction policy to lower-priority jobs to free ~6 GPUs. Will run at 1778610300.

maya: Reverting note: if hosted p95 > 500ms we should revert routing. Currently p95 hosted = 320ms.

infra-oncall: TL;DR — dedicated eu-west2 exhausted; automated spillover working but causing some hosted latency and a handful of 504/429s. Mitigations in flight: route flip for non-enterprise, mute noisy jobs, manual evictions, cloud quota request. Will update thread when cloud approves or when we see sustained stability. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sophie: Update at 1778610600 — noisy job muted, queue depth stable, hosted errors down to baseline. Cloud quota ticket created (ticket RI-2026-487). I'll follow up with cost estimate for bursting vs reserved capacity.

ajay: Confirmed manual eviction freed 6 GPUs at 1778610455. Dedicated pool utilization now 74%.

infra-oncall: Thanks team. Postmortem to follow if cloud quota not increased within 48h. Marking incident as 'mitigated' for now. :white_check_mark:
